title: Large-deformation plasticity and fracture behavior of pure lithium under various stress states

nodes.label: Lithium-metal cells need a quantitative large-deformation and fracture description of pure Li

attrs.note: no introduction in the packet; the need is domain knowledge about Li-metal anodes

nodes.label: Li's plasticity and fracture over stress states from simple shear to triaxial tension are unmeasured at the meso-scale

requires_unseen: 'meso-scale gap that needs to be bridged' in the Fig. 9 linked text

nodes.label: Battery-grade 750 um Alfa Aesar Li foil (99.9%), specimens taken parallel to the rolling direction

requires_unseen: 750 um foil thickness
99.9% metals basis, Alfa Aesar
all specimens cut parallel to the rolling direction

nodes.label: Cut specimens with a 1064 nm laser through a sealed argon chamber of two glass slides, so the Li is never unsealed

requires_unseen: 20 W 1064 nm Electrox Scorpion G2 laser
chamber assembled in an Ar glovebox and kept sealed during cutting

nodes.image_note: the schematic shows the two slides, the Li sheet, the two rubber spacers, the o-ring and four binder clips, and the gap above the foil; it does not show the argon, the laser or the cut

nodes.label: Five specimen geometries span the stress states: uniaxial tension, central hole, notched R10, notched R5, simple shear
nodes.image_note: five dimensioned outlines: plain dogbone 5 mm gauge width, 10 mm gauge with a 2.00 mm central hole, R10.00 and R5.00 notches cutting 10 mm down to 5 mm, and a stepped shear coupon; whole figure read, no panels offered

nodes.label: Laser-cut the five specimen geometries from the foil inside the sealed argon chamber

requires_unseen: cutting done in argon rather than dry air

nodes.label: Load each geometry to fracture at 2.4 mm/min with DIC strain measurement, at least three repeats

attrs.condition: displacement rate 2.4 mm/min, uniaxial strain rate 4e-3 /s, room temperature
requires_unseen: 2.4 mm/min displacement rate
Instron 5944 with a 100 N load cell
DIC extensometer between the marked points

nodes.label: The as-received rolled foil has equiaxed grains of order 100 um, so a gauge section holds only 10-30 grains

requires_unseen: the specimen gauge/characteristic length of 1.5-5 mm, about 10-30 grains (Fig. 9 linked text)
attrs.text_value: 107 um mean with 49 um standard deviation, log-normal, ~500 grains (text)

nodes.label: Laser cutting leaves a heat-affected layer only about 50-100 um deep at the cut edge
Deformation runs by slip: straight traces of two active slip systems inside single grains, stopping at the boundaries

requires_unseen: the statement that slip lines are oriented differently in individual grains and stop at the grain boundaries (Fig. 6 linked text)

nodes.label: Wavy slip lines identify cross-slip as active already at room temperature, as expected for Li's low melting point

requires_unseen: lithium's low melting point, so that room temperature is already a high homologous temperature (Fig. 6 linked text, k3)

nodes.label: Grains thin continuously until the local thickness reaches zero and the fracture surface collapses to a line
Pure Li fails by perfectly ductile fracture: separation by sliding, no dimples, no crack initiation in shear
Engineering stress peaks near 1.2 MPa at about 0.05 nominal strain and then falls monotonically: strain hardening is small
Through-thickness plastic strain grows about four times faster than width strain: strong through-thickness anisotropy

attrs.text_value: Lankford r = 0.138, giving F = G = 0.879 and H = 0.121 (text)

nodes.label: Rate strengthening is significant: without it the material loses the load-carrying capacity the test retains after necking
Small hardening drives localisation, raising the local strain rate 3-10x; rate strengthening then resists it, and the balance sets Li's ductility

requires_unseen: local strain rate reaches 3x (tensile tests) and ~10x (notched necking) the nominal rate, from the simulations

nodes.label: Fracture displacement falls as the stress state becomes more triaxial: about 3.4 mm (R10), 2.4 mm (R5), 2.0 mm (central hole)
A notch or hole imposes triaxial tension at a fixed section, so failure is forced there instead of at the weakest point

requires_unseen: the argument that an un-notched specimen fails at its weakest point, e.g. a material imperfection

nodes.label: A transverse-isotropic Hill48 model with Voce hardening and rate dependence, calibrated on four tests, reproduces all five force-displacement curves

attrs.condition: inverse calibration on central hole, notched R5, notched R10 and simple shear; uniaxial tension kept as validation
requires_unseen: the inverse calibration used central hole, notched R5, notched R10 and simple shear, with uniaxial tension kept back as validation (Fig. 7 linked text)

nodes.label: Pure Li is perfectly ductile from shear to triaxial tension; small hardening, strong rate strengthening and through-thickness anisotropy set its large-deformation response
The measured peak stress of about 1.2 MPa is roughly 50% above the ~0.8 MPa reported in the literature

requires_unseen: literature maximum stress of about 0.8 MPa, refs 19 and 38

nodes.label: The simulation still cannot reproduce the thickness reduction to zero; localisation into one element row makes it numerically unstable

requires_unseen: the statement that incremental deformation localises into only one or two elements

nodes.label: Both through-thickness anisotropy and rate dependence must be kept: isotropy over-predicts the force, rate independence predicts premature collapse
With air exposure the surface reaction products go from isolated particles to linked chains across the grains
Air exposure up to 10 min leaves the stress-strain curve unchanged; after 60 min the peak stress rises to about 1.4 MPa
Only once the reaction products link into a network do they carry load and stiffen the specimen; isolated particles do not

requires_unseen: the statement that isolated particles merely stick to the surface without being linked

nodes.label: Keep air exposure short and test under argon or a plastic bag, so oxidation does not enter the measured response

requires_unseen: the statement that the plastic bag contributes no measurable stiffness

nodes.label: The 99.9% Li carries no second-phase particles that could nucleate voids

requires_unseen: 99.9% metals basis purity
the statement that no defects were available for dimple formation

nodes.label: Hill48 anisotropic yield function with Voce hardening and a power-law rate term; ten parameters, four fitted

requires_unseen: the model form and the ten-parameter count
the Nelder-Mead inverse-calibration procedure in Abaqus/Standard

notes: Spine (19): n1 need -> n2 gap -> DES n3/n4/n5 -> PRC n6 -> n7 -> STR n10/n12 (+MEC n11) -> PRP n13/n14/n15/n16 -> MEC/tradeoff n17 -> PRF n20 -> DSC n21, with a second branch n7 -> n18 -> n19 for the triaxiality series. Control branch (spine false): air exposure n25 -> n26 -> n27 -> n28, linked to the main line by n26 contrasts n14. Audits (3): n9 (heat-affected zone qualifies the measured force level, the linked text names it as one of three contributions to the rising shear force), n22 (1.2 MPa vs the ~0.8 MPa literature value) and n23 (thickness reduction to zero not reproduced). Node count 50 is above the 25-40 aim because the packet carries 12 figures, all of which were opened. Packet defects: (1) figure ids run ahead of the paper's figure numbers from F7 on - packet F7 and F8 are the two parameter tables with empty captions carrying Fig. 7's linked text, so packet F9 = paper Fig. 7, F10 = Fig. 8, F11 = Fig. 9, F12 = Fig. 10; (2) F9 is tagged C3_caption_swap but its caption does match the image, the real fault being the two empty captions before it; (3) the OCR letter for F4d and F6d reads 'p' instead of 'd'; (4) F4b, F4c, F10a and F10b are recorded with no cue classes and 'scale bar: False', although F4c plainly carries a 10 um bar; (5) the F4b OCR mangles the y-axis label into 'IPa'/'tres'. Information lost: the constitutive equations, Tables 1-2 beyond the numbers read off F7/F8, the DIC local fracture strain of ~400%, the dynamic-recrystallisation softening argument of the Fig. 9 text, and the F4a, F6c and F11a/F11b panels (opened but not cited).
